record.:question/problem:
Consider the equation in the variable $v,$ given by

$$
3nv=6v+6
$$

where $n$ is a constant. Given that this equation has no solution, what is the value of $n?$
record.:question/worked-solution:
Suppose we have an equation of the form

$$
ax=b
$$

where $a$ and $b$ are constants, and $b\ne 0.$ If $a=0,$ then the equation has no solution.

First, we rewrite the equation in the form $av=b.$ 

We start by subtracting $6v$ from both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}3nv & =6v+6 \\ 3nv-6v & =6v+6-6v \\ 3nv-6v & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we factor $v$ on the left-hand side. This gives

$$
(3n-6)v=6.
$$

Notice that this equation is now in the form $av=b:$

$$
{{(3n-6)}_{⏟}}_{a}v={{6}_{⏟}}_{b}
$$

Therefore, the equation has no solution if

$$
3n-6=0.
$$

Solving this for $n,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3n-6 & =0 \\ 3n-6+6 & =0+6 \\ 3n & =6 \\ \frac{3n}{3} & =\frac{6}{3} \\ n & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
